newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: U.S. presses Saudis for more cooperation on bombing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. presses Saudis for more cooperation on bombing.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Sunday pressed Saudi Arabian leaders to provide more information to the FBI in the investigation of a terrorist bombing in Saudi Arabia last June that killed 19 U.S. troops.

Cohen told reporters following a meeting in Jeddah with Crown Prince Abdullah and Defence Minister Prince Sultan that Abdullah replied that "full cooperation would be given" in the incomplete Saudi bombing investigation.

The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation has complained about a lack of Saudi help on the unsolved truck bomb blast at Khobar Towers military housing complex in Dhahran last June 25. No blame has been assigned for the attack and no determination made on whether an outside country sponsored it.

"I don't have the specifics of what the FBI needs. But I just indicated that they felt that they needed more information. And he (Abdullah) indicated that ... full cooperation would be given," Cohen told reporters aboard his aircraft en route to Kuwait from Jeddah on the second leg of a Gulf visit.
"He responded that it was in all of our interests -- their interests as well as our interests, to give as full cooperation as possible, that anything that needed to be done he felt would be done."
Cohen said he had "reiterated what President (Bill) Clinton had said, that we expect full cooperation and we expect we will receive it".
